newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zapatista rebels released from Mexican jail on bail.
newsitem.headline: Zapatista rebels released from Mexican jail on bail.

text.p: Seven alleged Zapatista rebels were released on bail from prison late on Friday after spending 21 months in Mexico's top security jail, a rebel sympathiser said on Saturday.

The sympathiser, belonging to the civic arm of the Zapatista movement that rose up in arms in the southern state of Chiapas against the government on Jan. 1, 1994, declined to outline bail conditions.

"Their release is a result of the social pressures brought to bear on the government and the amount of bail does not matter," said the spokesman from the Zapatista National Liberation Front (FZLN), requesting to remain anonymous.
It is standard for jailed Mexicans to be released on bail after serving only part of their sentences because of the shortage of penal facilities.

Although the seven never admitted belonging to the Zapatista fight for land and indigenous rights, the release of captured rebels is one of five key Zapatista demands before they return to stalled peace talks with the government.
Freedom for the seven from Mexico's Almoloya Jail, the country's only top security prison from which no one has ever escaped, means only 10 alleged Zapatistas remain behind bars.
Mexico started its fiercest clampdown on alleged Zapatista rebels on Feb. 9, 1995, sweeping across various states in a bid to quell growing support outside Chiapas for the rebels.
Since the intital bloody uprising, in which at least 145 people were killed, there has been little fighting between Zapatistas and the army.

Peace talks between the Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) and the government were called off in September after 18 months of wrangling. Rebels claimed the government was negotiating in bad faith.
Attempts to coax the rebels back to the negotiating table are bogged down in discussions on how the peace discussions should be held.
